verdict.rationale: Trigger.dev ships an official SDK, `@trigger.dev/sdk`, that provides all v3 functionality, including a programmatic management API (e.g. `runs.list`) and task triggering that returns handles you can use to check status, cancel and retry. A community report notes some docs and examples still show deprecated v3 code after the v4 transition, which is a documentation-quality caveat rather than a contradiction. Missing for 10: evidence of official SDKs beyond TypeScript/JavaScript (Python is only mentioned as a build extension), a published OpenAPI spec (probes returned 404), and independent hands-on corroboration of SDK depth.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can build against official SDKs

citations.quote: All `v3` functionality is provided through the `@trigger.dev/sdk` module.
This triggers the task and returns a handle...You can use the handle to check the status of the task, cancel and retry it.
